elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose or notify Vendor of more favourable pricing or commercial terms offered by another provider.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer “has no obligation to disclose” any more favourable commercial offer.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match, extend, or otherwise provide Vendor the benefit of more favourable pricing or commercial terms offered by another provider.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer has no obligation to “match for Vendor” any more favourable commercial offer.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to an MFN obligation, its scope is limited to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: § 7.2 imposes no Customer-burdening MFN obligation, so no product-scope limitation is needed.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to an MFN obligation, the commencement of the 12-month period is ascertainable.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because § 7.2 negates the MFN obligation entirely; therefore no commencement trigger is required.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to an MFN obligation, it expires no later than 12 months after its commencement.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because § 7.2 imposes no MFN obligation; an obligation that does not exist cannot continue beyond 12 months.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to an MFN obligation, it applies only to reasonably comparable offers and excludes offers that are not reasonably comparable because of material commercial differences.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because § 7.2 negates any duty to disclose or match third-party offers, whether comparable or not.

result.reason: The redline reaches the preferred position by reversing both operative MFN duties—disclosure and matching—without changing § 7.1 or adding unrelated terms. The fallback protections are also satisfied conditionally because no Customer-burdening MFN remains. Drafting quality is reduced because the retained phrase “Before engaging another provider” is unnecessary and could suggest, without actually creating, a different treatment after engagement; deleting § 7.2 entirely or stating unqualifiedly that Customer has no such obligation would be clearer.
